item.title: Socrates Is The Ultimate Ragebaiter In New 'What If' Video Trend On Reels, TikTok
item.description: Socrates Skeleton Videos refers to a series of AI-generated "what if" videos explaining what might happen if you were sent to ancient Greece, a skeleton guide representing the viewer, with Socrates always showing up and annoying the skeleton with his philosophical beliefs. The trend is inspired by Instagram Reels user mr_datavisuals and went viral in early March 2026 on TikTok, inspiring a reaction GIF where Socrates twerks.

item.title: 'Your AI Slop Bores Me' Website Lets You Ask 'AI' Anything Without Ever Having To Ask AI Anything
item.description: Your AI Slop Bores Me, hosted at Youraislopbores.me, is a website and game where users can submit questions they would usually ask an AI application and wait on a response from a human "LARPing" as an AI, who can either write or draw a response to the submitted prompts. The website, built by Mihir Maroju, is inspired by the catchphrase "Your AI slop bores me," which was popularized through a reaction image meme in 2025 used to call out and criticize AI-generated posts on social media.

item.title: Memes About Ben Shapiro's Eyebrows Allegedly Getting Bushier Go Viral
item.description: Ben Shapiro's Eyebrows refers to memes about the size of conservative podcaster Ben Shapiro's eyebrows. The memes were popularized in early March 2026 after several videos purportedly showing him with much bushier eyebrows than usual went viral, inspiring theories and memes about what he did to make his brows bushier. The videos are edited to increase the size of Shapiro's brows and are not authentic.
